about: Sensitivity checks for the Round 1 pressure index. The primary (submitted) lists are the no-exclusion lists. Nothing here changes the primary method or the primary lists. Regenerate with `node sensitivity.mjs` from the data folder.

primaryCheck.description: Primary (submitted) lists as computed here (scoring.mjs on analysis_data.json, no player exclusions, 60 balls / 8 matches).

poolSizes.note: Eligible players per format-season pool, no exclusions (the submitted setting), 60 pressure balls / 8 matches / 60 ordinary balls. A pool with 10 or fewer players is flagged thin. Each player is standardised (z-scores) only against the others in the same pool.

method.leaveOneOut: Drop one eligible player of the same kind (all his records as a batter, or as a bowler), re-rate everyone with scoring.mjs, record the rank of every primary top-10 player other than the dropped one. A dropped player ranked above a top-10 player lifts that rank by one, so the best rank here is mechanical; the worst rank and the exit count carry the information.
method.bootstrap: 1000 resamples. Within each player-format-season group, the player-match records are drawn with replacement to the same count (a match-level cluster bootstrap), then everything is re-rated with scoring.mjs including the 60-ball / 8-match gate. This measures sampling noise in a player's own results (the primary top-10 players have 71 to 1048 pressure balls) together with its effect on the pool z-scores, so it is a wider test than pool size alone; poolDeletion is the pool-only test.
method.poolDeletion: 1000 runs. In each run a random 20% of the eligible players who are not in the primary top 10 are removed (11 batters, 25 bowlers), then everything is re-rated. The top-10 players' own data is untouched, so this isolates how much the make-up of the pools matters.
method.fragilityRule: Share of runs with the player in the top 10: fragile below 50%, moderate 50% to under 80%, stable 80% or more. `fragility` uses the bootstrap share (a player's own sampling noise and the pools together); `poolCompositionFragility` uses the random pool-deletion share (only who else is in the pools changes).

minimumPoolSize.note: Sensitivity only. A pool is dropped for one kind (batters or bowlers) when it has fewer eligible players than K; the players' records in that pool then contribute nothing (their reliability is also computed without them). The primary lists are unchanged.

poolingSeasons.note: Sensitivity only. Two ways of pooling seasons. standardisationPooled keeps every player-format-season profile and the same eligible players, and only changes the pool the z-scores are taken against (several seasons share one pool), so it isolates the pool-size effect; it ignores differences in scoring environment between seasons. careerPooled merges a player's seasons into one profile per format, so the 60-ball / 8-match gate applies to the merged career and many more players qualify; it mixes the pool-size effect with an eligibility change.

otherAlternative.assumption: Primary: an `other` delivery is an illegal ball (not one of the six legal balls) and the bowler is charged one penalty run, as for a no-ball; the run also counts in the innings score used for the required rate. Alternative shown here: still an illegal ball, but no penalty run is charged to the bowler or added to the innings score.

exclusionsOff.scenario: no exclusions, `other` = illegal ball, no penalty run

exclusionsOn.scenario: exclusions on, `other` = illegal ball, no penalty run

exclusionAlternative.note: The alternative to the submitted lists: same method and thresholds, with the three exclusion groups applied (the 53 Pakistan T20I players, the five IPL retirees, Mohit Sharma). Columns are the same as the primary tables; versusPrimary compares with the submitted (no-exclusion) lists.

otherEvidence.source: ball_by_ball.csv, all rows (the file also holds competitions outside the IPL / T20I scope)

overLength.note: Legal balls in an over = rows in that over minus the rows known to be illegal (wide, Overstep), and minus the `other` rows in the "illegal" case. The last over of each innings is excluded because it can be cut short.
overLength.earlierReportFigure: methodology_report.md says seven or more legal balls in 244 overs; this recount gives 243 (of the 254 overs with an `other` row, the other 11 are shortened last overs of an innings).

runMarginCheck.note: Matches decided by runs, with no byes, leg-byes, penalty rows, super over or revised overs, where the winning margin should equal innings 1 total minus innings 2 total (bat runs + 1 per wide and Overstep). The method is first checked on matches that have no `other` row.
runMarginCheck.verdict: inconclusive: the check does not reproduce the margin in many matches that have no `other` row, so it cannot decide the penalty question

inScopeEffect.note: Pressure deliveries in the 837 in-scope matches with the penalty run (primary) and without it.

summary: 264 rows have extras_type 'other'. extras1_runs is 5 on 264 rows; for wide it is 2, for Overstep 1, for ordinary balls 6.
Batter runs are recorded on 136 of the 264 'other' rows (26 sixes, 42 fours); on Overstep rows 337 of 576; wides never carry batter runs (0 of 7714).
3 'other' rows carry a wicket: 3 RunOut. For Overstep rows: 5 RunOut.

254 overs contain an 'other' row. If 'other' were a legal ball, 243 of them would have more than six legal balls (216 of the 216 that are not the last over of an innings); treated as illegal, 243 have exactly six (216 of 216 not-last overs). Overs with no 'other' row have exactly six in 100.0% of 30410 finished overs.

No row says how many runs the 'other' extra is worth: 'runs' is the batter's runs on every extras type, so the +1 penalty is a rule-based assumption (a no-ball costs the bowler one run), not something read from a column. Run-margin check: inconclusive (5 of 11 calibration matches reproduce the margin; 1 match with an 'other' row qualifies, and its margin 61 equals the difference 61 with the penalty run and 60 without it).
In the in-scope data the penalty run adds 70 pressure deliveries (81736 to 81806).

exclusionFlip.summary: One line in scoring.mjs switches the player exclusions on. The submitted lists use no exclusions. The change is `false` to `true` on the APPLY_PLAYER_EXCLUSIONS line.
exclusionFlip.checkDescription: sensitivity.mjs applies this exact edit to a copy of scoring.mjs in memory and confirms the batter, bowler and all-rounder lists equal the exclusionAlternative lists in this file.
exclusionFlip.whatTheEditDoes: Keeps the format and season filters and applies the three exclusion groups: the Pakistan T20I players, the five IPL retirees and Mohit Sharma. The dashboard imports scoring.mjs, so it shows the exclusion-filtered lists as soon as the line is changed. The text lists of the submitted names (the report, README.md, index.html) do not change by themselves.
exclusionFlip.analysisDataNeedsRegenerating: No. The exclusions are applied in scoring.mjs after analysis_data.json is built, so do not run analyze.mjs for this change.
commands: 1. In scoring.mjs change `const APPLY_PLAYER_EXCLUSIONS = false;` to `const APPLY_PLAYER_EXCLUSIONS = true;`.

2. node sensitivity.mjs --print-top10   (prints the top-10 batters and bowlers that scoring.mjs now gives; they must equal exclusionAlternative.batters.top10 and exclusionAlternative.bowlers.top10 in sensitivity_data.json, which holds the full metrics).

3. Do not run `node sensitivity.mjs` or `node charts.mjs` without arguments while the line says true: both describe the submitted no-exclusion lists and stop with an error. Change the line back to false before rebuilding sensitivity_data.json or the charts.

4. Report: methodology_report.md, methodology_report.html and methodology_report.pdf are written by hand (the PDF is the html printed to PDF). The exclusion-filtered lists with full metrics are already in the report section "Alternative: top 10 lists with the exclusions applied". To submit them, move those tables into the top-10 section, update the exclusion text, and print the PDF again.

5. Static text that also mentions the exclusions: README.md, index.html (method step 06) and the exclusion paragraphs in the report. The Unstop dropdown entries must be changed to the exclusion-filtered names.
